question: Which established HMC/NUTS remedy is justified for a 2018 model that failed a predeclared zero-divergence gate, and what one candidate can be tested in a matched follow-up?

already_noncentered: pooled raw standard-normal multiplied by HalfNormal scale
correlated cycle raw standard-normal multiplied by Cholesky factor
final race StudentT raw multiplied by final_race_sd
community drift raw normal innovations cumulatively summed
model_inspection.coordinate_location_limit: Flagged and nearby nonflagged controls have similar leading coordinate families and standardized magnitudes; this does not establish a causal geometry mechanism.

unchanged: same exact model/provider and factor targets
same eight protected parents and original masses
same NUTS implementation, backend, runtime and device
all diagnostics gates, including zero divergences and zero depth saturation
predeclared_candidate.prediction: If discretization error materially causes the retained divergences, smaller adapted step sizes at target 0.995 may remove them, with reduced efficiency possible.
predeclared_candidate.falsification: Any retained divergence or any other existing conditional diagnostic gate failure means C1 does not qualify; no further target tweaking is included in C1.

technical_sources.relevant_section: NUTS API; target_accept_prob lines 599-602 and adaptation/mass options lines 586-599 in web-rendered version
technical_sources.claim: Increasing target_accept_prob reduces adapted step size and trades speed for robustness; NUTS supports step-size and mass-matrix adaptation and diagonal/dense/block options.
Higher target acceptance/smaller step can help in some cases; varying curvature may require reparameterization.
Centered/non-centered hierarchical reparameterization is a geometry-sensitive option, often useful when data are weak.
Primary geometric treatment of HMC failure and divergence diagnostics.

scope_limits: This does not diagnose the cause or bias of the 76 divergences.
No actual model reparameterization is chosen without successful owner geometry results.
A higher target acceptance proposal is not evidence it will remove all divergences.
The original zero-divergence gate is unchanged.
